title: Genius idea to handle the risk of your game being copied and put on Roblox
author: Codingology
selftext:
If your game trailer got more than 10 likes there’s already a chance someone might vibecode it in Roblox and add ton of microtransactions.

Since this phenomena has gotten insanely viral, it’s safe for you to assume that your game IS going to be copied, if you believe it’s a good game at least.

How to combat this? 

Simply be you the guy who creates the Roblox slop version of your own game.  
When you are ready to deploy the official game you should already have done the slop one on Roblox studio, and release the Roblox version shortly after announcing to the public the original game.

You’re welcome

replies.body: Yea makes sense. I made this post for people who have a very interesting and innovative concept for a game. I’ve seen often straight adults saying “seems fun, gonna wait to play it for free on Roblox”

replies.author: Neither_Berry_100
replies.body:
Perhaps. But it still wouldn't be fast to make. Not without vibe coding and likely stealing my ideas and code.

Lots of my game mechanics and philosphies behind the game are easily understood. The mechanics can be duplicates easily. The philosophies will take work.

I have at least one critical game system which is quite substantial. It is extremely rare. Almost one of a kind. Doing this well and quickly would likely mean reverse engineering my game.

The graphics aren't super high fidelity so I'm sure they could get that or similar into roblox.
